forecast.question: Will available money cover the coming months?
forecast.needInputs: Enter available money, monthly income and expenses to calculate the scenario.
forecast.assumptions: Monthly scenario from {{month}}, in {{currency}}. Suggested income and expenses use three complete months; known one-off income is excluded. Review all assumptions.
forecast.starting: Starting funds after goals and committed bills
forecast.notReached: Not reached in the selected period
forecast.limitations: A what-if, not a prediction. Expenses stay fixed and already include debt payments. Reserve is part of starting cash. Exclude goal funds and committed bills from starting funds; do not also enter those bills as extra expenses. Add only new expenses not already included. Actual records are unchanged; drafts reset when the month or currency changes.
forecast.invalidInputs: Check the assumptions: amounts must be nonnegative, income loss 0–100%, expense increase 0–300%, duration 0–12 whole months, and the expense month within the horizon.
forecast.confirmSource: Confirmed account availability at {{date}} · {{currency}}. Starting funds {{starting}} include the designated reserve {{reserve}}; goal funds {{goals}} and committed bills {{commitments}} are excluded.
forecast.importEditable: Imported into this scenario; all assumptions remain editable. Later confirmations do not overwrite your edits.
forecast.confirmUnavailable: To import, confirm all account balances and currencies for the same closed month as this scenario.

period.hint: a month can also be picked on the chart

finding.overspentUsual: {{period}}: expenses exceeded income by {{net}}; usually {{usualRate}} of income is saved.
finding.expenseUsual: Expenses as in a usual month.
finding.expenseBelow: Expenses are {{amount}} below a usual month.
finding.expenseBelowPerMonth: Expenses are {{amount}} a month below a usual month.
finding.expenseAbove: Expenses are {{amount}} above a usual month.
finding.expenseAboveTop: Expenses are {{amount}} above a usual month, most of all {{category}} {{delta}}.
finding.expenseAbovePerMonth: Expenses are {{amount}} a month above a usual month.
finding.expenseAbovePerMonthTop: Expenses are {{amount}} a month above a usual month, most of all {{category}} {{delta}}.

expenses.title: Where the money went
expenses.coverage: Expense categories start in {{start}}: {{count}} of {{of}} months of the period here, {{amount}} of {{total}}.
expenses.noCompare: No comparison: there are no categories before the period.
expenses.empty: Expenses of {{period}} are not split by category.
expenses.track: Mandatory, loans, by choice and unsplit expenses
expenses.meta_one: {{total}} · usual is the median of {{count}} month before the period
expenses.meta_other: {{total}} · usual is the median of {{count}} months before the period
expenses.noRate: A line has no exchange rate: its amount and the shares are not counted.

category.usual_one: Usually {{usual}}: the median of {{count}} month before the period.
category.usual_other: Usually {{usual}}: the median of {{count}} months before the period.

income.title: Where it came from
income.coverage: Income categories start in {{start}}: {{count}} of {{of}} months of the period.
income.oneOff: One-off income {{amount}} ({{names}}) is not counted in forecasts.
income.loans: Loan payments count to the loan's owner.
income.empty: Income of the period is not split by category.

capital.title: What changed in net worth
capital.restNote: “The rest” is what income and expenses do not explain: rates, revaluation of property and investments, repaid loan principal (expenses hold the whole payment), corrections.
capital.label: Net worth change: saved from income and the rest
capital.empty: No net worth at the end of the month before the period: nothing to compare with.
capital.more_one: {{count}} more; all records together {{total}}. A loan balance is “plus” when it went down.
capital.more_other: {{count}} more; all records together {{total}}. A loan balance is “plus” when it went down.
capital.total: All records together {{total}}. A loan balance is “plus” when it went down.
capital.closedOnly: Records are broken down only for the last closed month.

categories.lead: Split each account's income and expenses by category.
categories.partial: {{month}} is not fully split: {{expense}} of expenses and {{income}} of income without a category.
categories.unknown: {{month}}: a line has no exchange rate, so what is left to split cannot be counted.
